articleTitle: Review of Exoskeleton: History, Design and Control
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: An Exoskeleton is wearable device that consists of mechanical structure, sensors, actuators and controller. This is widely used in various engineering applications such as to enhance endurance and strength of soldiers and assisting the patient with walking disorder. In view of this, paper brings out brief history of the Exoskeleton and their design. Further, study of different control aspects used in major augmented type Exoskeleton is also carried out. Finally, future challenges have also been discussed.

articleTitle: Modulated Perturb and Observe Maximum Power Point Tracking Algorithm for Solar PV Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this work, a Modulated Perturb and Observe (MoPO) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm is proposed for the solar PV array, where a uniform solar irradiance on solar PV array is considered. For MPPT on solar PV array, several techniques have been proposed, where the most popular technique is `Perturb and Observe (P&O)' MPPT technique. However, there are issues with P&O MPPT technique like fix step change, the oscillation in the steady-state condition and large tracking duration during dynamic change condition. In this paper, these issues are mitigated by using a modulated step change, which shrinks the size during the steady-state condition for reducing the oscillation and expands the size during dynamic irradiance change condition to quickly capture the new MPP (Maximum Power Point). The performance of MoPO MPPT technique is evaluated on different types of solar irradiance condition, as well as its dominance over the state of the art techniques is proved through a comparative study with classical P&O MPPT technique.

articleTitle: Recent Trends in Automation-A study of RPA Development Tools
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Robotic process automation is an smart way to manage work across those machines which AI can easily be categorize. Robot Automation is a sequence of steps that gives result in a meaningful action without interference of human being. In any organization, Robot automation can perform tasks just like a human being. RPA is a program in which sequence of commands are executed as per the predefined rules of organization. When any organization change its rules then either it needs to hire new employee those can work with new rules or it have to provide training to existing employees to map the requirements of new rules. These both ways are time and money consuming. By the use of Robotic automation, the company can place effective workers those can do an impression of human workers.

articleTitle: PSO Optimized PID Controller Design for the Process Liquid Level Control
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In modern industrial applications, the process liquid level needs to be maintained at a pre-defined level to achieve higher efficiency and final product quality. For uninterrupted electric power generation, the boiler tank water level has to be continuously controlled and monitored. The Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) is commonly used in such processes to attain better response. The PID Controllers have lesser development costs, superior features and yields in better system output. In this paper, the PID gain terms are tuned by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The PSO has simple concept, implementation is simple. The process liquid level control of a plant by conventional PID and PSO optimized PID controllers has been analyzed and quantitatively compared. The computer simulation results show far better settling time and peak values with PSO optimized PID control, thus ensuring overall higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparison of Advance and Conventional Motors for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to offer a comparison between the traditional motors with advance motors. At past, DC motors were popular for electrical vehicles but advancement in technology makes PMBLDC based motors become popular. These all motors are radial motors. Now a day's all conventional radial motors like PMBLDC and induction motors are replaced by axial PMBLDC and induction motors. The first part of this paper compares conventional motors like DC Motor, induction motors, radial PMBLDC motors and SRM Motors with their torque-speed characteristics.. The second part of this paper compare the advance axial flux motors with conventional radial flux motors with simulation results.

articleTitle: Food Spoilage Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks and K Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the novel idea for detecting food spoilage using image classification with machine learning algorithms and artificial intelligence technology. Food spoilage is detected by using artificial intelligence, deep convolutional neural networks, and computer vision and machine learning algorithms like k clusters algorithm for color classifications in images and its HSV values for spoilage detection. This project is done using the jupyter notebook platform through anaconda prompt. In this project, photos of food or fruits will be taken which have to be tested and then it will be processed through computer which will then perform image classification and machine learning algorithms for getting the colors in the image and spoilage is detected by HSV (Hue Saturation Value) values and percentages of each color which we have got by using the k cluster algorithms in jupyter notebook.

articleTitle: Impact of Solar Photovoltaic Penetration In Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The integration of Renewable Energy Generation to the grid steadily being growing due to environmental awareness, green energy evolution and incentives from the government. Most of the RES integrated to the distribution system in the form of distributed Photovoltaic(PV). As seen from the last few years the integration of PV at residential distribution network increases rapidly and it is expected to further increase in the penetration level with growth of RES, causing some undesirable impact on the distribution system such as over voltage, voltage fluctuations and reverse power flow to the grid. A IEEE 13bus test case by EPRI has taken for the distribution system impact analysis in terms of voltage performance and system losses. The distribution system is modelled in the OpenDSS (Open Distribution System Simulator) and interfacing has done with MATLAB to investigate the effect of PV penetration at the distribution system. A comparative study of with and without PV is shown and several PV integration scenarios are discussed with different penetration level. Further mitigation methods are proposed to overcome the power quality.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Sources Integration in Micro-grid including Load Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The research paper presents an implementation of Microgrid. A new concept which assumes lots of loads & sources operated under a one controllable unit system which provides heat & power to the localized area. Various existing models of sources are used to describe the microgrid's components. A complete model is built which includes microgrid, power sources like Wind energy, Solar Energy, Diesel generator models inbuilt in MATLAB/Simulink. A new combination of these models is tried to analyse the impact of integrating the renewable energy sources with microgrid. Various quantities like active power, reactive power, apparent power, current & voltage are analysed for Wind farm, Diesel generator, Solar PV farm and that of loads are shown and presented in the research paper. The various factors on which production of energy depends are PV farm's size & it's efficiency and speed of wind for Wind farm.

articleTitle: Malicious Node Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks are basically a collection of sensor nodes scattered in a large area such that the desired information can be collected. But sensor nodes are also vulnerable to the attacks such as malware, hackers, faulty hardware or from the physical phenomenon etc. Hence, it is mandatory to protect a sensor node from an attack because if it gets attacked then the information sent by the sensor could be wrong and lead to incorrect data analysis and hence can lead to unnecessary outcomes. In this paper, a technique based on machine learning to discover malicious nodes within a randomly deployed sensor network has been proposed. Here, Support Vector Machine for time series prediction has been employed to find the malicious nodes based on the past values acquired by those individual nodes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Model for Brain Tumor Segmentation & Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Gliomas are the most hostile among brain tumors and other known cranial ailments. Patient with high-grade Gliomas often results in diminished life span. In an attempt to provide a solution, we propose a brain segmentation model for tumor detection which could be considered an appropriate tool for medical image processing. Due to the presence of an enormous quantity of magnetic resonance scanned images, performing cancer diagnosis by lab scanned images becomes quite laborious and hand-operated segmentation for brain tumor becomes complicated and slow-moving chore. One reason for its complexity could be explained by the fact that, these tumors have high probabilities of materializing in any part of the human brain without having defined size or shape. The aforementioned problems fueled our research to built a novel approach using deep learning which utilizes both global as well as local features of medical imaging for precise segmentation. In our research, we have implemented and tested Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based models for detecting brain tumors by utilizing the concept of deep neural networks. Our proposed deep learning model combines Two-Pathway and Cascade architectures to analyse and implement brain segmentation. These models are used for segmenting Gliomas of both types. Our results are evaluated over Input Cascade and outcomes showed better performance than existing MFC Cascade.

articleTitle: Microgrid System for A Rural Area - An Analysis of HOMER Optimised Model Using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: There have been many methods of attaining a suitable combination of renewable energy sources. This work analyses the stability of one such system optimised by HOME-Rquickstart for a small community at Gurmia, India; on the occurrence of faults. The chosen location has a fair potential of solar and wind energy, trapping of these resources efficiently in the form of hybrid microgrid systems could solve major power issues and in the same time supersede the old grids. This work involves simulation of an optimised model obtained from HOMERquickstart package using Simulink. Various cases are considered in interlinking of the energy sources for the microgrid and their respective transient behaviour in the occurrence of faults are observed.

articleTitle: FEM Based Study of Short Circuit Forces on Power Transformer Windings
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The transient current in the transformer winding leads to deformation of core and winding. This paper examines the electromagnetic force and winding deformation occurring in the transformer due to short-circuit current. Axial and radial forces are generated in the transformer winding which leads to its distortion. This work aims to study about these mechanical forces and analyse its effect on a 3-phase, 3 leg, 66/11 KV transformer. Finite element analysis is done on a 40 MVA power transformer with the help of COMSOL Multiphysics. The study is important for designing the transformer in such a way to keep the damages originated due to abnormal conditions like faults and other transients at the bay. The electromagnetic force study is important for manufacturing and operational consideration.

articleTitle: Sensitivity based ATC Maximization by Optimal Placement of TCSC applying Grey Wolf Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The deregulation of the power industry resulted in the participation of the private sector, which reduced the rates of electrical supplies to end-users but on the other hand it increases the congestion in the power system due to overloading of the transmission lines. To mitigate congestion many cost-free and non-cost free methods are used. Congestion in the power system can be minimized effectively by enhancing the Available transfer capability (ATC) of the transmission line. This paper demonstrates sensitivity-based analysis to enhance ATC by incorporating TCSC on the standard IEEE 30 Bus system. Sensitivity factor ACPTDF is used to search the location of the device and the size of TCSC is optimized by the Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm (GWO). The detailed method to locate and optimize TCSC for reducing system power losses and increasing Available Transfer Capacity (ATC) is demonstrated in this paper. The utility and superiority of GWO are illustrated here on the system and are detailed with the help of a suitable table and figures.

articleTitle: Modelling of Solar parabolic trough collector considering Unsymmetrical Heat Flux
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Concentrated solar power is one of the ways to convert solar energy into process heat or electricity. Now a day's different types of collectors are available but Parabolic Trough Collector (PTC) is used in the current study. The basic working principle for this type of collector is that it receives the parallel solar rays on the collector after reflection converges linearly on the absorber tube which is a circular pipe through which the fluid flows and thus solar energy is transferred to the fluid. The solar energy is thus utilized in heating the fluid flowing in the absorber tube. The solar radiation effect after the reflection from the collector has been modeled using the Monte Carlo Ray Tracing technique (MCRT). The heat flux is uniform in the longitudinal direction of the tube but it varies in the circumferential direction of any axial location. Most of the authors used constant heat flux on the collection tube. The current study aims to apply the unsymmetrical heating load over the absorber tube of PTC to perfectly simulate the actual condition.

articleTitle: Determination of faults in 3–Ø Induction Motor By Motor Current Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Induction machine is horse power equipment for industry. It is widely used as drive of many industrial processes but their unexpected failure can cause heavy production loss. Motor current signature analysis (MCSA) is monitoring a parameter of condition in machinery viz the instantaneous current which contain all frequency contain for identification of characteristic fault signature at early stage for avoiding unexpected failure like rotor defect (fragments of rotor bar), stator fault and air-gap peculiar fault. This paper present detailed analysis of how fault frequency is inducing as byproduct of unique rotating flux components and how fault frequency is modulated in stator current which was not done so far. The MCSA Simulation is done by using MATLAB R2017a/Simulink.

articleTitle: Hybrid Optimization Model for Smart Grid Distributed Generation Using HOMER
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: For sustainable development, the energy policy of every nation has been changed significantly to allow high penetration of renewable energy in the power grid and especially in the distribution network. On the other hand, the utilization of a single renewable resource is associated with power quality and stability issues so the hybrid renewable energy system can be seen as a possible solution to this challenge. In this paper, a hybrid optimization model is designed and purposed for a university campus, which depicts a commercial load profile. The hybrid model comprises of solar-PV and biomass as renewable energy resources and the HOMER software is used in this study for simulation of the hybrid model for optimization and sensitivity analysis. The numbers of configurations are simulated in the HOMER and most cost-effective configuration is determined. With the implementation of this model, the Levelized Cost of energy is reduced from Rs. 6.2/kWh to Rs. 4.7/kWh and it is found that grid imports are reduced by 86.67%.

articleTitle: Emerging trends in Electric Vehicle in Indian market
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: With growing concerns about the environment and receding fossil fuel reserves, the world is moving towards sustainable fuels and modes of transport. One of the forerunners are battery operated electric vehicles and fuel cell based electric vehicles. In this paper, we discuss about the electric vehicle market scenario in India, electric vehicle supply equipment and globally available chargers (for both AC and DC). An economic model is proposed for setting up EV charging infrastructure at a mall in India based on recent regulations introduced by the Government of India. We discuss about its feasibility and in turn try to motivate private and semi-private bodies to come together in order to setup more charging stations, hence encouraging the boom of EV industry in India.

articleTitle: StudieMe: College Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this work, we present a novel web platform for a college selection process. Having a recommendation system as a helping hand to give them detailed information about the options they have and the best options to choose from according to their caliber is a huge requirement. In this paper, we worked on a designing a recommendation system that could understand the skill set and interest of a user through the data from the User's Profile to suggest recommended options of colleges for the users to select. We have developed the college recommendation system as a web platform which gives the result as top matched colleges for a particular user.

articleTitle: PMSG based WECS with MPPT via modified P & O algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Gearless wind energy conversion system based supplies can be a long term solution in case of distributed generation. This paper validates a modified control algorithm for maximum power point tracking of Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based wind energy conversion system. This work aims to optimize the losses by extracting maximum wind energy. Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator is used as it provides gear free mechanism, low noise and it's easy to control. DC-DC boost converter has been used for implementing MPPT by controlling the duty ratio. This ensures effective utilization of wind energy. In this work the instantaneous values of input side current and voltage are used for implementing MPPT. Modified (P&O) algorithm is used which is more efficient as compared to its traditional counterpart. It reduces the problem of unsettlement around the peak point. The whole work is verified in MATLAB/ Simulink environment by carrying out simulation for the proposed work.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Pulmonary Emphysema by Congregating Statistical Features
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a pulmo disease that is distinguished by reduction of peak expiratory flow rate and steady forced discharging of lungs. Pulmonary emphysema is one of the causes of COPD, and is due to damage in alveolar sacs that is caused due to loss in its elastic quality. An early diagnosis and it's treatment could help to take steps in controlling the symptoms. Hence, the quantification of emphysematous lesions in alveolar sac has been a significant topic of research. However, visual evaluation of computed tomography(Ct) images faces the challenge of being a tedious work and relies solely upon trained radiologist. Hence, an algorithm is proposed that would provide a reliable and automatic system that would end the dependence of radiologist and also aid in lessening time to accurately classify between normal tissue (NT), centrilobular (CL) and paraseptal (PS). The proposed novel method quantifies emphysema by congregating features: statistical features of wavelet transformed image, grey-level co-occurrence matrix(GLCM), first order texture statistical features and grey-level run length matrix(GLRLM). To validate the presented algorithm, leave-one-out cross validation technique was employed on the CT database. An accuracy and sensitivity of 91.67% and 91.89% was achieved. The specificity and precision of 95.72% and 92.22% respectively was obtained.

articleTitle: Impact of FACTS Device on Zonal Protection Scheme in Modified Dorsey-Chicago Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Distance protection scheme used conventionally over lines for faults detection requires adaptability to the system variation. This paper develops an approach using shunt connected Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) based devices. The Static VAR Compensator (SVC) is used as integrated part of power system with fault detection using distance relay characteristics. Simulation is developed on PSCAD and results are generated and validated using fault impedance analysis at different location of protection scheme control phenomena in presence of SVC. The mho characteristics are observed for under/over reach phenomenon for accurate detection of the fault, when connected system due to presence of (SVC) FACTS. The device impacts on line impedance characteristic presented to relay for faults (LG, LLG and LLLG) are simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Power Quality Improvement for Non Linear Load Applications using Passive Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Design and analysis of various filters for harmonic filtering purpose becomes very significant with increase in penetration of distributed generation system to a utility grid. Many researchers have developed various filtering techniques over the last few decades. In many literatures emphasis is given on the various power harmonic filters like passive filters, active filters and the hybrid filters. According to various circuit configurations and their harmonic compensation capabilities focus has been provided on both passive filters as well as active filters. In modem electrical energy distribution systems, maintaining good power quality is a challenging issue because poor power quality cost enormous amount of economic loss. In this paper, passive filters are the topic of interest because of their robust filtering techniques based on their configurations, type of connection as well as location in the power grid. Here the parameters of different passive filters are estimated and a complete harmonic analysis is provided. This paper highlights the relevance of passive filtering techniques in specific areas like harmonic compensation in nonlinear load applications.

articleTitle: Robot Operating System Integrated robot control through Secure Shell(SSH)
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The paper presents the operation of a robot through SSH. The robot is a disaster rescue robot and is ROS integrated. Through SSH the robot's CPU is accessed from a robot operating console. Commands are passed from the console to the robot's computing unit through SSH. These commands are used to execute the already existing programs in the robot's processing unit and transmit the results to the operating console through wired or wireless communication. Different programs were executed and their results were presented in this paper. The communication between operating console and robot's CPU is established using a high bandwidth router to avoid the delay in data transmission.

articleTitle: Smart soil nutrients analysis and prediction of the level of nutrients using a bot
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In today's world, there is an increase in population growth. Fertilizers are being used to increase crop productivity, but for producing more crop, nutrient level of soil and crop monitoring is more important. This is one of the main factors for the production of rich and good quality crops and also helps the farmers to determine the type of crops to be planted on his land. Our system is such, which measures the pH, NPK(Nitrogen, Phosphorous, and Potassium) values of the soil and the soil moisture using the respective sensors. The system also uploads this data on the ThingSpeak cloud so that the readymade generation of the data set is possible for the machine learning.

articleTitle: Qualitative Analysis of CMOS Logic Full Adder and GDI Logic Full Adder using 18 nm FinFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this paper we qualitatively analysed basic full adder circuitry, which is implemented using CMOS technology (28T) and GDI technique (10T) using 18nm FinFET technology. The primary objective is to optimize our conventional adder so that an experimental analysis is conducted in order to analyse these two distinct circuits with same operation in terms of Area, Propagation Delay, Power and Power-Delay-Product (PDP). All experimental analysis is carried using Cadence Virtuoso (cds-ff-mpt library is used for FinFET).

articleTitle: Recent techniques in MEMS to design a sensor for Energy Harvesting: A Review
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In recent years concern for harvesting energy from the freely available sources which can be used on chip with the portable electronic devices eliminating batteries. This paper reviews on geometries of one such sensor that can be used for energy harvesting from freely available ambient vibrations. Changes in geometries and designes of sensor and thickness of layers in these designs ultimately affect the output voltage which can be used to power devices. This EH sensor works on principle of indirect piezoelectric effect. Hence along with changes in geometries of cantilever beam also various piezoelectric materials like ZnO, AlN are used in sensor. To further improve the voltage output changes in existing architecture, material and dimensions of sensor is required.

articleTitle: Wavelet Mutation based JAYA Optimization Algorithm for Global Maximum Power Peak Searching for Partially Shaded Solar PV Panel Condition
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this manuscript, a novel `Wavelet Mutation based JAYA Optimization (WMJO), algorithm is developed for GMPPS (Global Maximum Power Peak Searching) for partially shaded solar PV (Photovoltaic) panel condition. In classical GMPPS algorithms like Particle Swarm Optimization, Differential Evolution, Genetic Algorithm, etc., the major issues are, longer searching time during dynamic change condition, and computational complexity. The mitigation of these issues is the key contribution of this developed WMJO algorithm. In WMJO algorithm, the searching particles are pushed towards the global maximum peak by JAYA optimization algorithm, and the concept of Wavelet Mutation (WM) is used to explore the solution space. Therefore, the hybridized form of JAYA optimization algorithm and WM, WMJO algorithm searches GMPP (Global Maximum Power Peak) very accurately, which enhances the GMPPS efficiency in a steady-state condition. Moreover, in every iteration for dynamic condition detection, here an envelope of power is created, where the range is 5% below the lowest value of worst power and 5% above the highest value of the maximum achieved power in that iteration. In dynamic solar irradiance change condition, the envelope of power detects the situation and accordingly explores the searching particles to quickly capture the GMPP zone. Both these tactics increase the tracking efficiency in steady-state condition as well as decreases the GMPPS duration in dynamic irradiance change condition. The performance of WMJO algorithm is evaluated on different types of characteristics of solar irradiance pattern, through MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Light Management System with Manual Control
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Congestion at road intersections is a widespread problem. Congestion is a result of improper management of traffic. To make this traffic management process less hectic and automated, Traffic Lights are used at intersections which are effective too. Various researches focus on making traffic lights more reliable and effective which include a) Survey System b) Induction Loops c) Proximity Sensors d) Image Classification. Every proposed technique computes the vehicle count using any technique and accordingly timing of lights is set. In this paper, a system has been proposed which primarily utilizes image classification and has three main parts: Vehicle Count using Image Classification, Decision making Algorithm and Manual Control. Real-time traffic is analysed using image processing and computed vehicle count is given as input to decision-making algorithm, in return algorithm sets the timing of green signal to a selected lane. The timing of signals can also be updated by utilising manual control unit of the system. The proposed system provides manual control to lights along with real-time analysis of traffic and performs 75% times better in comparison with the survey system.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of TRMS using FO-PID and FOI-PD Controllers: An Experiment
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The emphasis of this paper is to develop and design the controllers in the modes of Fractional Order- Proportional Integral Derivative and Fractional Order Integral- Proportional Derivative for stabilization of benchmarked Twin Rotor Multiple inputs multiple-output system (TRMS). These controllers have been implemented and compared experimentally for the trajectory control of TRMS. Both the controllers are explained, and their parameters are reformed and tuned by using the interior-point nonlinear optimization method (fmincon function) to minimize the cost function of controller parameters. The pitch and yaw trajectory responses of TRMS with both the controllers are experimentally obtained and tested with disturbances at different intervals. It's observed that Fractional Order Integral-Proportional Derivative controller will provide effective trajectory tracking as compared with Fractional Order- Proportional Integral Derivative controller.

articleTitle: Wide Band Transimpedance Amplifier using Class AB FVF
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: CMOS technologies have swiftly ameliorated across the past few years. To meet the demand of high performance applications like compact disc players, high definition television (HDTV), radar, medical imaging etc., this employs info conversion system for processing at later stages. Accuracy is highly desirable in many functional systems like optical communication, military surveillance etc. In optical communication system, transimpedance amplifier (TIA) is the fundamental part of optical receiver which is required to convert the low level current signal from the photodiode to an operable output voltage for further processing. Here in this paper, we propose a CMOS TIA using class-AB flipped voltage follower having less output resistance. Simulation results of the proposed circuit in 0.18μm technology depicts that the bandwidth and the transimpedance gain obtained are increased by 3.3 times and 1.03 times respectively.

articleTitle: Smart LED Streetlighting System with Improved Power Quality and Low Standby Consumption
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This paper describes the main characteristics of an 80W constant current smart LED driver which works in 6LoWPAN mesh networking. The power supply capable to drive LED voltage of very wide output range (60V-110V) as well as a wide input range (90V-300VAC) with very high displacement power factor and very low input current distortion power factor. The free band radio range limitation is overcome by using 6LoWPAN mesh network to control light remotely using microcontroller and SubGHz wireless module. The standby consumption of power supply is less than 500mW which follow EnergyStar norms set by international agency.

articleTitle: Orbit Transfer using Optimal Control Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Main objective for the orbit transfer problem is optimal minimization of time and fuel. In this research, 2-body system is represented by a nonlinear dynamic system. Theoretical analysis of Euler-Lagrange and Hamiltonian function is implemented for the application of optimal control. Certain assumptions are taken into account such as continuous thrust acceleration for the entire interval, unbounded control variables, and presence of certain state variables designated at terminal boundary conditions. These provide solution for the orbital transfer between 7000 km circular orbit and 8000 km circular orbit, which are coplanar in nature, by uniting a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) and the Shooting method. For determining indirect optimal results about fuel or time, obtained results are compared with the Hohmann transfer. It is observed through the numerical simulations that the optimal theory applied coplanar rendezvous maneuver is optimally comparable to the minimum energy solution.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Isolated and Non-Isolated Bi-Directional DC-DC Converters for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative analysis is done between two bi-directional DC-DC converters i.e. transformerless and with transformer. Traditional batteries are unidirectional and large in size but bi-directional DC-DC converter (BDC) interconnected between battery and 400V DC bus provides wide voltage gain ratios and facilitates power flow in buck mode (charging) and boost mode (discharging). Energy storage is required in isolated microgrid in order to save power during OFF-load period and to deliver when excess loads are connected; therefore it is necessary that battery must be bi-directional. This bi-directional battery has applications in nanogrid or microgrid for energy storage, electric heavy vehicles, uninterrupted power supply, etc. The two BDCs are modeled, simulated, controlled and operated in different modes using MATLAB/SIMULINK. The results of comparison using various criteria are discussed in this work.

articleTitle: Towards Development of a Portable Apparatus for Knee Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The knee is the most commonly injured part of the human body. This paper aims to design a portable knee health apparatus by picking up muscle signals and angles. It consists of an EMG circuit to sense the muscle activity and an IMU sensor for measuring the angle. These two muscles are useful for movement of the leg. The quadricep of the leg is made up of four muscles one of the muscles is vastus medialis which is involved in the flexion extension activities along with tracking of patella, the calf muscle of the leg whose half compromises of the gastrocnemius is used for plantar flexing of knee and ankle joint. The dynamic movements such as running, jumping and other fast movements of the leg are dependent on the gastrocnemius muscle. This approach is applied to the different age groups of people especially on people above 60 years of age both males and females and adults above 20 both genders. By using the two parameters i.e. muscular strength and angle of the leg, we differentiated the knee with abnormalities and without abnormalities. The above two parameters were taken at four dynamic positions i.e. sitting-standing and flexion-extension. The results showed good potential for the non-invasive diagnosis of knee health.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of SDBR and R-Type SSFCL for Enhancement of Low Voltage Ride-Through Capability of Wind-Farms
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The stability of a Grid greatly depends on the fault recovery process of wind farms. A variety of different Fault Current Limiters (FCLs) have been investigated by the researchers. Inclusion of FCL leads to enhancement of Fault-Ride Through (FRT) capabilities of the system. The Grid Codes (GC) are developed with incorporating Low Voltage-Ride Through (LVRT) as one of the obligatory requirement for integrating wind farms with the Grid. In this paper the response of wind farms to a fault occurrence has become very important to study grid stability. Various grid codes have been defined for this purpose and Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT) has been given as one of the major requirements for integration of the wind farms to the grid. In this paper, a simulation study has been done with Resistive-type Solid State Fault Current Limiter (R-SSFCL).The results are compared with Series Dynamic Braking Resistor(SDBR)to check the qualitative performance of proposed FCL. The proposed R-SSFCL has been found to give better-quality Fault Ride Through (FRT) capabilities which can be attributed to maintaining LVRT at faulty situation. The graphical results obtained from simulations show that the proposed FCL effectively improving the FRT-capabilities.

articleTitle: Implementation of Fuzzy based on Second Order Sliding Mode Controller fed Induction Motor Drive for Disturbance Rejection Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this method it shows a unified approach which deals with fuzzy based sliding mode controllers (SMC) is used for Asynchronous drives. In this paper it deeply focuses on the matched and unmatched disturbance and the expressions which will be derived and by using some rules it can be eliminated. By analyzing it shows the basic disadvantage of hysteresis (SM of order one) controllers these limitations can be improved on controllers having higher order. Fuzzy based Second order sliding mode controllers (SOSMC) will be analyzed and the disturbances can be eliminated and system is free from chattering. This shows that the drive having Fuzzy based SOSM controllers regulates the steady switching frequency and they maintain decoupling between torque - flux occurring at the same time. If any disturbances occur by which sudden change in speed and load, or by variations in parameters. The performance of the system which improves the time varying response at high sampling rates with switching frequency constant. The simulations were implemented in Mat lab/Simulink.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy based Second order sliding mode control(SOSMC)

articleTitle: Sensor Based Quality Check and Automated Fuel Level Indication System
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Aiming to build a comprehensive system for the safety and convenience of vehicle users so as to determine the nearby petrol bunks in case of fuel emergency, to determine the quality of petrol and also, it is proposed, to let the user know the amount of pollution being caused by the vehicle and if a pollution check is required. In this paper the fuel level present in the vehicle is detected with the help of a distance sensor and provides the nearby petrol bunks on Google maps. It is also proposed to let the vehicle user know the quality of petrol, based on its density, and also to alert him for a timely pollution check with the help of a semiconductor sensor.

articleTitle: Maintenance of DC Link Voltage using Synchronous Reference Frame Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This paper implements a control strategy based on d-q axis theory or synchronous reference frame theory (SRFT) for the control of power electronic converter connected to a grid. The control objectives of this paper are to develop a Simulink model using SRFT as the controller and to maintain a constant dc link voltage for any variation in load and for any type of load. A constant DC link voltage is required for the synchronization of input side (generating side) and output side (grid side) and this is done using the SRFT controller as presented in the paper. The control technique SRFT as presented is preferred due to ease of implementation and provision of instantaneous compensation of the reactive power.

articleTitle: A New Multilevel Inverter Topology with Minimal Power Electronics Component
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Multilevel inverters are widely used in high power and high voltage applications. These inverters have many advantage over two-level inverters in terms of harmonic contents, voltage stress, electromagnetic interference etc. But, it has some disadvantage as increased number of power electronic switches, driver circuits and voltage sources. A new cascaded multilevel inverter topology has been developed with a focus to overcome all the disadvantages mentioned. In this topology number of switches required in current path for a level in output voltage has been reduced and also requirement of other parameters are also reduced. Therefore, the overall cost and the space for installation is reduced as compared to traditional topologies like Cascaded H-bridge, Flying Capacitor, Modified H-bridge inverter and series connected inverter etc. Proposed multilevel inverter structure can generate 127 level in output voltage by using only three basic unit in cascading manner. The performance of the proposed structure has been verified for 31-level inverter using MATLAB/SIMULINK and differen simulated waveforms are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: FPGA Implentation of JPEG Image Compression
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Image compression is important in various applications such as video networking, medical images, and multimedia applications where a large amount of data transmission, storage is necessary. The main aim of the Image Compression technique is to reduce the redundant data so that it can be transmitted and stored efficiently and there is no significant change in the quality of the image. This paper introduces the design of the JPEG image compression and decompression algorithm and its simulation using the software Model Composer. Each block of the JPEG Algorithm was coded and designed as IPs. These IPs were integrated into a complete system along with some built-in blocks in Model composer. Performance of the system is measured using parameters Peak Signal to Noise ratio (PSNR), Compression Ratio (CR) based on file size and data rate. These parameters are recorded and compared with images of different sizes and formats.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of Reduced Switch Topologies of Multilevel Inverter Using Various PWM Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Recently, multilevel inverters have turned out to be common because of their ability in voltage activity and capacity. The multilevel inverter acquires near sinusoidal output from numerous dc voltage sources by utilizing a switching frequency. In this paper, a case study has been done with some newly recommended multilevel inverter (MLI) topologies with reduced number of power switches. An attempt has been made to compare them using various SPWM methods. Comparison and analysis is shown on the basis of total harmonic distortion (THD) with PD, POD, APOD applied to various topologies of seven-level inverter. As the proposed topologies have been suggested by different researchers for different applications, each configuration has its own benefits and limitations. Further, a compromise has to be made between number of switch count, complex modulation strategy and power quality.

articleTitle: Bistatic Coverage Driven Assessment of Proposed Space Radar Constellations
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is a moving platform-based radar imaging processing system. In order to provide day-and-night imagery, the Space-borne Radar Systems (SRS) is a recommended United States Defense SAR system. There are multiple open-source methodologies for analysis that consider distinct multiple SAR constellations in terms of cost, performance, and the global coverage. Nevertheless, analysis of all of the prior proposed constellations lacks assessment in terms of bistatic potentiality. Bistatic SAR can efficiently deliver 3D imagery which a monostatic operation system lacks. The current analysis presented in this research looks at the existing constellations along with the newly proposed constellation concerning the coverages which are monostatic as well as bistatic in nature. It is deduced that the 2 constellations with equal satellite count vary with regards to the performance when one for monostatic coverage is compared to another for bistatic coverage. Based on observations, a constellation is recommended comprising of 2 constellations of Walker 5/5/1 type which are offset in terms of Right Ascension of the Ascending Node (RAAN). On comparing with standard Walker 9/3/1 constellation, suggested constellation satellites, total count of 10, delivered analogous monostatic coverage, however, much enhanced b istatic c overage is also observed. Augmenting the relevance of analysis, presented examination also illustrated the significance of monostatic coverage along with bistatic coverage while developing a SAR satellite system.

articleTitle: Design of an Improved Q-ZSI with Fault Tolerance for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this paper, a Fault Tolerant Quasi Z-source Inverter (Q-ZSI) topology has been proposed for three phase induction motor drive systems. The proposed topology incorporates the ability to detect an open circuit or a short circuit fault in any of the switching arms. Once a fault is detected the firing signal is transferred to another switching arm to ensure uninterrupted flow of power. The main goal of this paper is to design a rugged inverter topology that can give better performance than the standard Z-Source Inverters (ZSI) in harsh environments where the switches are more prone to faults.

articleTitle: BLDC Motor Based Solar Water Pumping System with Grid Interface
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This work mainly focuses on solar PV fed water pumping system using Brushless DC (BLDC) motor. When compared to induction motor, BLDC offers higher efficiency, improved power factor, reduced size and better power density. Since solar PV is unreliable source for continuous power flow instead of using batteries, grid is chosen as other source of supply. As the output generated by solar PV changes in proportion to input irradiation, improved P&O based maximum power point tracking technique is implemented. To utilize the motor pump to its full capacity and to share the load demand between the two sources power factor controlled converter circuit using dual loop average current control approach is implemented here with improved reliability. MATLAB/Simulink environment is used for simulation of the chosen system under various test conditions namely at constant, varying and zero irradiation.

Author Keywords: solar water pumping system Induction motor

articleTitle: Design of Low Power Full Adder Circuits Using CMOS Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: 1-bit different full adder circuits are designed using CMOS technique for low power consumption and less delay. These are implemented using Cadence Virtuoso at 180nm technology for 1.8V supply voltage. The parametric constraints such as power consumption, delay, area are compared with designed different full adder circuits and commented on which design gives best performance parameter. Power Delay Product defines the efficiency of the circuit. As low power design is the main research in VLSI, hence design the circuits which require low power, less area, less delay. The performance of complete design appertains to the performance of full adder circuit design.

articleTitle: Power Spectrum Estimation of PMU using Digital Signal Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Synchronous phasor measurements are important parameter for wide-area monitoring and control applications. The main application of signal processing in the area of power systems is to determine the parameters to be measured and up to what level of accuracy. The purpose of this study is to compare various methods of Signal Processing for Phasor Measurement Unit through MATLAB and to find which signal processing methods provide the best characterization and analysis of the signals to be investigated.

articleTitle: Optimal Allocation of Distributed Generation for Power Loss Minimization using PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The rapidly increasing demand for electrical power and difficulties in providing the same using traditional power generating sources provide a motivation to integrate distributed generation (DG) into the radial distribution network. In the proposed work, the ideal arrangement of DG is investigated in IEEE standard 33-bus radial distribution network for minimizing network power losses and simultaneous node voltage profile upgradation. The load model chosen is constant complex power. The power flow solution with DG incorporated is computed using the Newton-Raphson algorithm under normal loading conditions. The optimal positioning and power rating of DG are computed by particle swarm optimization approach. The methodology proposed is verified by comparing it with the loss sensitivity method and the analytical method. The significantly reduced network power losses and significant improvement in node voltages is observed which shows the efficacy of the methodology proposed.

articleTitle: Digital Ticket Booking and Checking Using Aadhaar Card or Fingerprint and Android Application
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In the current system, we can get ticket both over the counter and online, but often we do not get ticket due to black-marketing and also it generates the paper ticket with the carbon printing. And in ticket checking process, there is lots of manual work to take place for maintaining passenger's records which is tedious to manage. To deal with these problems, this paper gives the solution by regulating ticket booking process using Aadhaar card no. or fingerprint which will reduce the use of carbon printed paper tickets and paper waste. We are developing an android application that will help the ticket checker to check the ticket and keep records effectively.

articleTitle: A Single Phase Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter Based STATCOM with Reduced Lower Order Harmonics for Railway Application
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The quality of the pantograph voltage is important for railway traction load. The nonlinear drive system of the locomotives itself distorts the line voltage. This can affect the performance of other locomotives connected to the same feeder. So it is inevitable that proper compensation should be provided to improve overall system efficiency. This paper aims at discussing the use of a Waveshaper based Modular Multilevel Converter (W-MMC) based STATCOM to improve the power quality of a single phase locomotive feeder by providing reactive power support and harmonic current compensation. The W-MMC based STATCOM uses less number of switching devices compared to a Cascaded H-Bridge Converter (CHBC) based STATCOM. The converter is simulated in PSACD/EMTDC software and the results show its effectiveness as a STATCOM. The converter generates lower order harmonics which may cause resonance with the existing passive filters in the network. A flux error compensation based method is proposed for the reduction of lower order harmonics. The proposed compensation method is also verified through simulation in PSCAD.

articleTitle: Comparison between Different MPPT Controllers for Solar PV Fed DC grid Connected Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In the work a study is performed between different maximum power point tracking (MPPT) techniques for DC grid connected solar PV applications. To harness the maximum power from available input under changing weather conditions MPPT controller is used. Different MPPT techniques namely Perturb and Observe (P&O), Incremental Conductance (In &C), Fuzzy logic and Random Search Method (RSM) based MPPT techniques are implemented here. Due to simple computation, absence of derivatives RSM guarantees global convergence, unlike other methods. Simulation is performed in MATLAB/Simulink environment to identify efficient MPP tracker.

articleTitle: Demand Side Management Using GUI
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: proposed work in this paper describe a software package tool by using MATLAB GUI for solving demand side management problem using load shifting technique. This helps user to improve the input data details in according to load used by the consumer and calculate the expenditure. This paper proposes software for load shifting consumption scheme to understate the peak demand and in turn save electricity billing. The load shifting technique of demand side management is used in this software for residential area to shift their load part from maximun to minimum hours with the help off time of the day tariff structure.

Author Keywords: Time of the Day Tariff Structure

articleTitle: Prediction of Optical Transmittance Loss In Solar Panels Using Lambert-Beer Law
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The energy industry is extensively using the photovoltaic generators. The output of the panels during day time depends on various parameters solar irradiation, temperature, wind speed, humidity, fog and dust deposition, etc. In the outdoor photovoltaic generators under the natural weather conditions, the deposition of dust particles and pollutants reduce the energy efficiency. The deposition rate of dust particles are highly dependent on characteristics of the aerosol, humidity, wind direction, geographical location, tilt angle and cleaning time of panel. The dust density keep on increasing with the exposure time if cleaning is not done regularly. The dust covering the solar cell glaze leads to the degradation in the light beam optical transmittance, which causes the shadowing effect and reduction in the energy conversion efficiency. In the paper, particles with different dust densities are considered and reduction in the optical transmittance recorded experimentally and mathematically. In the study, dust particles of 4.2 to 1.4micrometer size are considered at different density level from 2g/m2 to 40g/m2. The paper provides the estimate of the number of particles present during different dust densities responsible for the optical transmittance loss. The results show that the transmittance is linearly decreasing in the initial dust densities, but after 20g/m2 the reduction is exponential and is followed by the saturation in transmittance. The result shows that the radius and density of the dust particles has a significant impact on the light beam transmittance.

articleTitle: Multiple Dispersed Generation Allocation using Analytical Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The extent of this study is to evolve a new analytical approach to determine optimal sizing and siting of distributed generation (DG) unit(s) within a power distribution network considering the power loss minimization. The developed analytical model is based on curtailing the real and reactive power losses with respective branch components of currents by allocating the DGs at discrete places. The proposed method first, sequentially recognizes the possible nodes, where DGs can be sited. Afterwards, the best DG sizes are estimated using the expressions of loss saving for active and reactive DG's components. In order to find out, the optimal locations for DG placement a computational algorithm is developed. Moreover, analytical expressions have been derived and formulated considering three cases for power loss minimization and voltage profile improvement with and without integration of DGs. The IEEE 69-test distribution network is used to test and validated the method. Results of each case are compared and demonstrated the best case for highest loss saving obtained by DG unit's allocations in the system.

articleTitle: Design, Modeling and Performance of Static Synchronous Series Compensator Regulated Self-excited induction generator
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Voltage regulation of Self-Excited Induction Generator (SEIG) deteriorates with the inductive load and loading. In this paper, the attempt is made to design, model and to improve the SEIG performance using self supported static synchronous series compensator (SSSC). Contrary to series capacitor method, the performance with SSSC is extremely improved. The modeling of SEIG is done in q-d frame. The SSSC model is developed in abc frame. The control technique of SSSC consists of dual proportional-Integral (PI) controllers, one is applied to maintain dc link voltage by producing reference in-phae SSSC voltage and other PI controller is applied to maintain the load terminal voltage by producing reference quadrature SSSC voltage. Hysteresis current controller is applied to produce the pulses for SSSC. The proposed control technique is simulated on developed model of SEIG-SSSC system. The system is tested for variety of three-phase inductive load with sudden loading and unloading conditions. The power quality of SEIG-SSSC system is also assessed by evaluating harmonic spectrum of generator and load side voltage and current. The Total harmonic distortion (THD) of SEIG-SSSC system is obtained to comply the IEEE 519 standard. Overall the system performance is found to be satisfactory.

articleTitle: A Robust Multilevel Security Mechanism against Geometric Attacks
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The need for secured data communication in today's world is a prime concern of every internet user facing various security assaults. To cope up in such a hostile environment, various researchers have proposed the use of multiple levels of securities which combine cryptography and steganography. The most common approach in literature uses spatial domain steganography technique coupled with symmetric key cryptography. Though, spatial domain steganography possess a rich PSNR value and a good perceptual quality however, it's robustness against geometric attacks is less. Therefore, this paper proposes a robust multilevel security mechanism which inculcates transform domain steganography technique combined with hierarchical visual cryptography. To enrich the data embedding capacity, Huffman compression is also added. The proposed mechanism is implemented in MATLAB-2012 and the result shows that the technique is far better against attacks than the other ones available in literature.

articleTitle: Wavelet Based De-noising of EEG Signal Acquired from Tele-serial Addicted Persons
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Tele-serials have several cognitive effects. It can be noticed that people are getting addicted to different kinds of television serials now-a-days. From the survey it is found that tele-serials have bad cognitive effects and it increases the negative behavior. Till now no significant study of the tele-serials on the effect of cognitive behavior based on technical parameters is done. In this work, the effect on cognitive performance is investigated based on the variation of alpha and beta relative band energy and entropy. EEG Data is acquired from the subjects using Mobita-32 channel wireless EEG data acquisition system. However the recorded EEG signal is contaminated with noise and needs to be de-noised before further analysis. Choosing a suitable mother wavelet function and smoothing method, removal of artifact noise is possible. In the proposed work different mother wavelets are implemented to select the most compatible one with the EEG signal recorded. The minimum mean square error (MSE) and higher signal to noise ratio (SNR) are the criteria chosen to determine the denoising efficiency. The features considered for examining cognitive performance are calculated before and after denoising process are shown in this work. Also the proposed work shows a significant variation in a person's cognition after watching tele-serials on a regular basis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control Algorithm for DSTATCOM in three phase four wire distribution systems for Power Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This adaptive control technique has been developed for four-leg VSC based DSTATCOM using MATLAB Simulink environment and implemented in three phase four wire distribution systems. In this technique three reference currents are estimated from fundamental active power component of three distorted load currents. The performance of DSTATCOM found satisfactory in terms of load balancing, power factor improvement, source current harmonic elimination, and self-regulated DC bus voltage using adaptive control technique under steady state and dynamic condition using nonlinear load.

articleTitle: Low Power and High Linearity Cascode CMOS LNA for BLE Applications in 45 nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Bluetooth Low Energy is advanced technology which was marketed by Bluetooth SIG for distinctive applications at 2.4-2.5 frequency range. This paper presents a low input reflection coefficient (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; -15 dB) and low power LNA using cascode stage with inductively degenerated technique in 45nm CMOS process technology. The LNA is optimized for working in Bluetooth Low Energy application i.e., 2.4GHz frequency range. Implementation of the circuit design was done in Advanced Design System (ADS) software. Cascode with inductively degenerated topology provides high gain, nominal noise figure, high linearity and low power consumption features. The low noise amplifier achieves low input reflection coefficient (S11) of -25.045 dB, maximum gain of matching circuit i.e., 21.154 dB, reverse transmission coefficient (S12) of -24.130 dB with nominal noise figure (NF) of 3.695dB at 2.4GHz frequency. The LNA achieves low power consumption 0.017mW from a 1V power supply.

articleTitle: Real Power Transmission Loss Minimization and Bus Voltage Improvement Using STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The modernization in all sectors has been resulted in terms of day-by-day continuously increased electrical power demand. Because of which, the challenges of heavy real and reactive power loss as well as voltage instability have been surfaced. In this paper, a shunt-type FACTS device known as STATCOM has been used to overcome these challenges. Keeping an eye on this, an optimal dispatch problem for reactive power is solved in presence of STATCOM. The real power transmission losses are minimized and the results are analysed for different loading situations in the standard IEEE 14 bus test system. All the simulations are carried out on DigSILENT PowerFactory software. The simulation results obtained which demonstrate the significant role of STATCOM in the real power transmission loss reduction and bus voltages of the power network.

articleTitle: A novel approach for detection and removal of High Impedance Faults in power system based on voltage parameter
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: A High Impedance Fault (HIF) is a condition that occurs in the power system when a power transmission line breaks physically and comes in contact with the ground. Such faulty conditions do not draw a considerable amount of current from the system and hence, these faulty conditions are not detected by the primitive overcurrent protection scheme. When the system is subjected to any kind of fault, then we must understand that the detection of such faults are very acute and their removal is also important. This paper presents the novel technique for detection and removal of High Impedance Fault based on the voltage values. The proposed technique has been tested on a 3 phase system, where a voltage sensitive relay has been designed constitute of digital devices, which detect the high impedance fault in the system. The result shows that the HIF can be detected instantly with high accuracy and these would be removed to protect the system.

articleTitle: Automatic Fault Diagnosis System for Voltage Source Inverter Driven Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The high power drives used in industries are bulky and expensive. Several motor drives are used for different processes in the same plant. A major fault in any one of the drive can stop the whole process and may result in huge monetary loss and may also damage the associated drives. Hence for proper functioning of the drives, it is necessary to monitor the performance and health of the drive which can be performed by condition monitoring. In the proposed work, a simulation model of a three phase, 415V, 50Hz VSI fed squirrel cage induction motor is developed in MATLAB Simulink environment and also a Graphical User Interface (GUI) is built using the MATLAB App designer platform. The model is simulated to analyse the system behaviour under healthy and faulty conditions and the GUI is designed to extract the simulation data, monitor the condition of the system and generate a diagnostic report indicating type, location and severity of the fault within the system.

articleTitle: Comparison of RL and LC Output Matching Networks for Cascode Inductive Source Degeneration LNA in 45 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This paper reports the designing of low noise amplifier (LNA) using the inductive source degeneration with cascode topology with different output matching stages namely resistive with inductive load (RL circuit) and inductive with capacitive load (LC circuit) in 45 nm CMOS process technology at 2.4GHz frequency. The implementation was done in Advanced Design System (ADS) software. The LNA obtained moderate gain of 5.046 dB, input reflection coefficient of -10.869 dB, maximum gain of 15.410 dB, and noise figure of 3.590 dB and with power consumption of 8mW for RL output matching network at 2.4GHz ISM band. For LC matching network, the LNA achieves high linearity 21.597 dB, high gain of 18.408 dB with low power consumption 2 mW, respectively.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation Control of Multi-Area Multi-Source Realistic System using GWO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This paper presents the study of an application of an innovative search method founded on the concept of artificial intelligence. It focuses on the factors to be optimized that is nonlinear in Load Frequency Controller (LFC). To study the given purpose, a power system with multiple sources is considered. Area-1 has non-reheat thermal, hydro and wind plants while area-2 has non-reheat thermal, hydro and diesel power plants. System performance with boiler dynamics and governor dead band (GDB), governor rate constraint (GRC) was also considered. Gray Wolf Optimized algorithm (GWO) is used to identify the optimum controller factors to mineralize time-domain-objective-function. The outcome obtained from its compared and analyzed with recently publishing algorithm outcomes viz. differential evolution (DE) and teaching-learning optimization algorithm (TLBO) to demonstrate the relatively better and more efficient performance of given scheme of tuning PID by GWO. With this correlative study and analysis, the performance of the proposed GWO is proven and verified over diverse operational settings, and system parameters disparities.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna with Superwideband Bandwidth Including Dual Notched Band Characteristics for UWB/X/Ku Band Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: In this manuscript, a MIMO (Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output) antenna is presented which encounters multipath interference loss of received signals. Also, proposed which is designed on Rogers RT Duroid 5870 substrate covers Superwideband bandwidth applicable for UWB/X/Ku band wireless applications. Two interferences, WiMAX and WLAN in UWB range is eliminated leading to dual notched band characteristics functional antenna. Tapered Microstrip feed provides larger matching of impedance leading to Superwideband. MIMO characteristics is studied by obtaining results related to ECC (Envelope Correlation Coefficient), DG (Directive Gain) and TARC (Total Effective Reflection Coefficient) which meets permissible values.

articleTitle: Importance Of Negative Phase Sequence Overcurrent Protection For Solidly Grounded Delta-Wye Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to discuss about the requirement of Negative Phase Sequence (NPS) overcurrent protection for solidly grounded Delta-Wye transformer and to provide guidelines to select the setting for NPS overcurrent protection. Currently NPS overcurrent protection is not used to protect the static device like transformers in any industrial projects. However for certain risk related to failure of protection equipment, only NPS overcurrent protection can provide backup protection to solidly grounded Delta-Wye transformers. Hence NPS overcurrent protection function can't be avoided in transformer protection relay at delta side of transformer. The comparison between all the transformer protections based on failure of certain protection equipment under fault condition is also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Technology Based Intervention to Improve Social Skills in Students on Autism Spectrum)
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The proliferating role of technology has given different hopes for increasing the lives of different persons with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Given study accessed the effectiveness of personalized Audio-Visual Social Story, a Computer-based Intervention. The paper highlights how Screen-based Technology can be used to enhance everyday communication and behavioral knowledge with decreasing aide from guardians, staff and therapists. Three persons having Autism problem, of different age and communication pattern were exposed to the stories developed according to the individual requirements. The subjects demonstrated reduced challenging behavior but the amount of improvement varied across them.

articleTitle: Effect of different shading Patterns on Photovoltaic Array Setups
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) energy generation is widely used now due to its ability to convert solar irradiation into electricity without any pollution. To get the desired output voltages and currents, various combinations of series and parallel connections of solar PV panels are used. They give optimum output during the fully shaded conditions. In partially shaded (PS) condition, the bypass diodes get activated and the total voltage of series connection reduces to lower value which results in to lower power generation than the desired. The output power varies according to the types of series-parallel combination, location of bypass diodes as well as the shade pattern. Hence, there is a scope to improve the output during this condition by choosing the proper PV panel configuration. In this paper, Series-Parallel (SP), Total cross-tied (TCT), Bridge-linked (BL) and Honeycomb (HC) configurations are analyzed for their shade resilience ability using Matlab/Simulink model.

articleTitle: Design and Development of finger probe for diagnosis of Anemia non-invasively
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: This present study describes the design of the finger probe to be working with near-infrared (NIR) and infrared (IR) light sources for the diagnosis of common blood disorder called as anemia non-invasively. The probe has been designed in 3D CAD system and fabricated with ABS plastic using Fortus 250mc 3D printer. In the probe the cushion has been used to provide comfort for the subject and flexibility to be used for all age groups of subjects (excluding children). Probe has been tested on multiple volunteers (male/female to record the neat and clean noise free photoplethysmographic (PPG) waveform. The output of the probe has been recorded using LabVIEW. The developed probe can be helpful to detect anemic conditions of the patient non-invasively which is a big concern now a days in society.

articleTitle: A Prediction Of The Temperature Of a Recessed LED Panel Ceiling Light
publicationTitle: 2019 3rd International Conference on Recent Developments in Control, Automation & Power Engineering (RDCAPE)
abstract: The recessed ceiling light emitting diodes (LED) lights or downlights are installed in a hole (cavity) in the ceiling of a building. The air surrounding LED circulates due to natural convection and carries heat from the LED light to the concrete. LED lights use electronic chips operated by a controlled direct current that is obtained from converting the alternating current to direct current by an electronic circuit.
